category_title: Students with learning disabilities who equate high-volume note-taking with learning and use abbreviations to increase speed
scenario_title: Managing note volume during a fast-paced science video lecture
minimal_context: Ben is taking notes on strategic note-taking paper during a 15-minute video lecture on Electro-Plasma Rockets to capture facts for future study.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: We are going to watch this 15-minute video lecture on Electro-Plasma Rockets. Please use your strategic note-taking paper to take notes while it plays.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Okay. I want to write down as many points as possible. Main points means facts, so I want to write more to learn off of.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Alright, I am starting the video now. Just do your best to take notes.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Writing quickly) I'm using abbreviations to increase my speed so I can record more lecture points. When you write a lot of notes down, you feel good about yourself.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: The video is moving to the next section. How are your notes coming along?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It's going too fast! I decided to work as fast as I can and write the words down that I wanted because the more work the better, but I'm struggling a great deal with writing fast enough. Forget about three to six main points, I want to put more than you’re supposed to do, but I can't keep up with the lecture!
